memos.headline: S06 Near Highs With Low Vol Leads the Board; S04 Overbought After Parabolic Move; S07 and S01 Weakest Relative Strength
memos.body: I see a clear split in this universe today. S06 stands out as the cleanest trend: just 0.5% off its 52-week high, +17.3% over 12 weeks, +12.5% relative strength vs SPY over that period, and ATR of only 1.89%—the tightest volatility in the group. S04 has been explosive (+29.8% in 4 weeks, RSI 78.1, +22.8% above its 50-day mean), which screams short-term exhaustion even though the relative strength is undeniable; I'd wait for a pullback toward the 50-day before getting involved. On the weak side, S07 is 20.9% off its high, 8.1% below its 50-day, RSI 42.9, and bleeding relative strength at -14% vs SPY over 4 weeks—this is a broken intermediate trend until it reclaims the 50-day. S01 is similarly weak: below both its 50-day and 200-day means, -12.8% drawdown, negative 26-week return, and persistent underperformance vs SPY. S03 looks constructive near highs with a 3.4% drawdown and strong 4-week relative strength, though the 12-week RS is slightly negative so I hold moderate conviction there.

views.note: Tightest vol in the universe, only 0.5% from 52w high, strong 12w relative strength of +12.5% vs SPY; would reassess on a close below the 50-day mean (~333).
RSI 78.1 and +22.8% above 50-day mean after a parabolic 4-week move of +29.8% signals near-term exhaustion; would turn long on a pullback toward ~407 (50-day area).
Only 3.4% off highs, +9.5% 4w relative strength vs SPY, RSI 64 in a healthy zone; invalidated below ~245 (200-day area).
Strong 1-week pop of +11.6% and only 5% off highs, but 12w relative strength vs SPY is -3.3% so momentum is newer and less proven; a close below ~206 (50-day area) would change my view.
Down 20.9% from highs, 8.1% below 50-day, RSI 42.9, and -14% 4w relative strength vs SPY—broken intermediate trend; need a reclaim above ~916 (50-day) to reconsider.
Below both 50-day and 200-day means, negative 26w return of -3.9%, persistent relative weakness vs SPY; would need a close above ~150 (200-day area) to revisit.
12% off highs, -8.5% over 12 weeks, and -13.3% 12w relative strength vs SPY—clear underperformer drifting near its 50-day with no upside catalyst in the tape.
Massive 26w return of +41.9% but now rolling over: -4.1% over 4 weeks, RSI 44, and -6.6% 4w relative strength; trend still above 200-day but near-term momentum is fading.

memos.headline: Hyper-scalers and AI semis dominate earnings power; legacy tech and low-margin names lag badly
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe. S10 posted 85% YoY revenue growth and a 71.5% net margin on $81.6B of revenue with only $8.5B of debt—the cleanest earnings profile in the group. S05 printed a 93.7% net margin on $119.8B of revenue with net income up ~298% YoY, which is extraordinary even allowing for possible one-time gains; I want to see whether operating cash flow confirms durability. S03 and S04 are solid compounders: S03 grew revenue 19.6% YoY to $200.6B with 31.2% net margins and S04 delivered 39.7% net margins on $90B of revenue with manageable $40.3B debt. On the other end, S09 and S02 are struggling—S09's net income fell 45.8% YoY to just $4.2B on a 4.9% margin, and S02 is barely growing revenue (+2.0%) with a thin 5.6% margin and $77.9B of debt. S01's earnings declined 15.8% YoY on anemic 1.5% revenue growth, and its 14.4% margin is under pressure. A sustained margin compression below 4% at S09 or below 5% at S02 would push me to outright avoid both.

views.note: 85% revenue growth, 71.5% net margin, and minimal $8.5B debt make this the strongest earnings-power story in the universe.
93.7% net margin and 298% net income growth are remarkable, though I need to verify operating cash flow supports the margin level before raising conviction further.
39.7% net margin on $90B revenue with 17.7% top-line growth and moderate $40.3B debt is a durable, high-quality compounder.
$200.6B revenue growing 19.6% YoY with 31.2% net margin is compelling at scale, though $133B debt warrants monitoring.
24% revenue growth and 65% net income growth with a 17.5% margin show improving earnings power, but $36.2B debt on $20.5B revenue is elevated.
27.7% revenue growth and 36.9% margin are solid, but $460.5B of total debt is an outsized liability that compresses equity returns.
16.4% revenue growth and 27.2% margin are respectable, but $82.3B debt and decelerating growth versus peers temper enthusiasm.
Net income down 45.8% YoY to a 4.9% margin on only 2.4% revenue growth signals serious earnings deterioration; I'd need margin recovery above 8% to reconsider.
Flat 2% revenue growth, 5.6% net margin, and $77.9B debt offer no margin of safety; operating leverage is absent.
Revenue grew just 1.5% YoY while net income fell 15.8%, and $29.3B debt on $21.2B revenue leaves little room for further margin erosion.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause at 3.75% but Sticky 3.5% YoY CPI and Rising Long Rates Argue Against Duration and Favor Defensive Positioning
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode—the upper bound has been flat at 3.75% for three months after 75 bps of cuts over the past year, and the effective rate at 3.63% confirms no movement. However, CPI running at +3.5% YoY (June print) is well above the 2% target, and the 10-year yield has climbed 42 bps over the past year to 4.65%, signaling the market is pricing in persistent inflation and potentially fewer future cuts. The labor market is stable with unemployment at 4.2%, down 10 bps over three months, which removes urgency for further easing. My regime call is 'pause with hawkish tilt'—this favors banks and energy over duration-sensitive growth and rate-sensitive sectors; a CPI print dropping below 3.0% or unemployment rising above 4.5% would shift me toward an easing regime. The flattening 10y-2y spread (now 0.44 pp, down 9 bps YoY) suggests the market sees limited further steepening, which caps bank NIM upside but still supports them relative to long-duration plays.

views.note: Rising long-end yields (+42 bps YoY to 4.65%) and a paused Fed with sticky inflation are hostile to duration-sensitive growth names.
Banks benefit from a positive and stable 10y-2y spread of 0.44 pp and a pause regime that keeps short rates anchored while long rates drift higher.
Energy tends to outperform in sticky-inflation, stable-growth regimes; 3.5% YoY CPI and 4.2% unemployment support the reflation trade.
Staples offer defensive value but limited upside in a pause regime where the economy is not yet slowing materially (unemployment only 4.2%).
Rate-sensitive sectors face headwinds as the 10-year yield climbs and the Fed shows no urgency to cut further with CPI at 3.5%.
Cyclicals are supported by a stable labor market (unemployment -10 bps over 3 months) and no imminent recession signal from the yield curve.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S03 and S04 Surge While S08 and S05 Sink on Results
memos.body: I am reading a clear bifurcation in earnings-season sentiment across the universe. S03 (+15.3%) and S04 (+15.5%) posted outsized positive price reactions to their 7/30 and 7/29 results filings respectively, signaling genuine narrative shifts that likely have further room to run as buy-side digests the numbers. On the negative side, S08 (-7.4%) and S05 (-7.1%) saw sharp sell-offs on their results, and with no subsequent positive catalysts filed through 8/7, the negative tone appears sticky rather than a one-day overreaction. S07's +5.6% move on its 8/4 earnings with Reg FD disclosure is fresh and constructive, though I have less conviction given the smaller magnitude. S09's 7/1 filing flagged a delisting notice alongside a complex restructuring, which is a distinctly negative narrative signal I would not fade.

views.note: A +15.3% earnings reaction on 7/30 represents a decisive positive narrative shift, supported by two prior Other Events filings that may have set the stage.
The +15.5% post-earnings move on 7/29 is the largest positive reaction in the universe and suggests a material upside surprise that sentiment hasn't fully absorbed.
A -7.4% earnings reaction on 7/30 with no subsequent positive filings through 8/7 suggests the negative tone is entrenched.
The -7.1% sell-off on 7/22 earnings is now two weeks old with no offsetting positive catalysts, indicating the market has repriced lower and sentiment remains negative.
A +5.6% move on the 8/4 earnings plus Reg FD disclosure is constructive and very fresh, though the magnitude is moderate.
The 7/1 filing flagging a delisting notice and material rights modification is a severe negative narrative signal regardless of the restructuring context.
High filing volume (7 filings in ~4 weeks) including a modest +2.5% earnings reaction and governance changes creates noise without a clear directional narrative.
A mild -1.9% earnings reaction on 7/29 paired with multiple Reg FD and officer-change filings is ambiguous; the tone is slightly negative but not decisive.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Rising but Credit Calm; WTI Spike Signals Energy-Supply Stress Worth Monitoring
memos.body: I see a divergence between the economic policy uncertainty index, which jumped 7.5% month-over-month to 262.24, and the VIX at 15.15 (down nearly 13% over three months), suggesting markets are not yet pricing the policy risk I track. WTI crude surged 13.3% in the past month to $78.88/bbl even as it remains 20% below its three-month-ago level, which I read as a short-term supply disruption or geopolitical premium re-entering the energy complex—this matters for energy-exposed names and downstream cost structures. High-yield OAS at 2.71% is essentially flat, so credit markets are not flashing distress, and the 10y-2y spread widening to +0.44pp is modestly constructive. Without specific GDELT event detail on sanctions or export controls, I have limited conviction on structural shifts; the 8-K filings across S01, S03, S06, S07, and S10 are generic Other Events or Reg FD disclosures that do not reveal direct geopolitical exposure. My view would change materially if new export controls targeting semiconductors or energy sanctions were announced, or if the policy uncertainty index sustains above 280.

views.note: Three Reg FD filings in two weeks suggest active investor communication but no geopolitical catalyst is identifiable from the evidence.
Four 8-K filings since late June indicate corporate activity, but absent detail on sanctions or supply-chain exposure I cannot take a directional view.
Two generic 8.01 filings offer no geopolitical signal; policy uncertainty is elevated but not yet at levels that warrant avoidance.
Recent Reg FD disclosure on Aug 4 is too opaque to assess geopolitical risk; holding neutral pending detail.
Single 8.01 filing in June with no follow-up; no identifiable geopolitical tail risk from available evidence.
With WTI up 13% m/m and policy uncertainty rising, energy-linked names may benefit if supply tightness persists; long on a tactical basis.
